items.summary: This repository provides the source code, simulation datasets, computational benchmarks, numerical results, and reproducibility materials supporting Paper I of the Principle of Representation Integration for Stable Models (PRISM-M), prepared for the Journal of Computational Neuroscience . PRISM-M V4 is a minimal recurrent computational framework organized around five functional operations: Extraction, Compression, Integration, Stabilization, and Prediction/Action (ECISP). The implementation uses a single independently evolving recurrent state, with finite-precision quantization and explicitly defined information-processing transformations. The framework is intended to examine the functional organization of information processing, contextual integration, and memory stabilization within established recurrent and state-space dynamics. The repository includes the frozen V4 implementation, mathematical definitions, parameter configurations, experimental protocols, random seeds, simulation trajectories, statistical analyses, and comparative benchmarks involving autoregressive models (ARX), Kalman filtering, and recurrent neural networks. The deposited materials document the original parameter-landscape and stability analyses, targeted perturbation experiments, memory-retention studies (M1–M5), and additional computational experiments (V1–V5) evaluating noise robustness, adaptability, recovery, interference resistance, and information recoverability. Additional validation materials include information-matched representation controls, intrinsic-noise sensitivity analyses, and mathematical verification of contraction and perturbation equivalence. These retrospective analyses are distinguished from the original experimental protocols. The repository also contains the numerical datasets, figure files, supplementary materials, execution instructions, software dependencies, provenance records, and SHA-256 integrity checks associated with Figures 1–6 and Supplementary Figures S1–S4. Computational reproduction and numerical verification have been performed for the principal analyses. Complete automated regeneration of all final publication artwork and independent cross-platform verification remain outside the scope of the completed checks. The purpose of this deposit is to facilitate independent evaluation, computational reproduction, and further investigation of the PRISM-M V4 framework. The model is a theoretical computational implementation and does not constitute direct biological validation or demonstrate a new class of recurrent dynamics.

items.summary: Supplementary data for "OpenScientist: evaluating an open agentic AI co-scientist to accelerate biomedical discovery." This dataset contains research logs, knowledge states, provenance files, and generated figures for seven case studies spanning neurodegenerative disease transcriptomics, multiple myeloma genomics, survival proteomics, drug side effect analysis, and more. Each case study includes the full agent iteration log, configuration, and final report. Input datasets are included for three case studies where data sharing is permitted: case study 3 (neurofibrillary tangle transcriptomics), case study 4 (multiple myeloma RNA-seq), and case study 7 (drug side effect frequencies from clinical trials).  Version 2 (August 2026) adds supplementary material for case study 3 (neurofibrillary tangle transcriptomics): 60 additional independent runs of the same question and dataset, comparing three agent/model configurations — Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.8, and the omp harness with Kimi K3 and GLM 5.2 — each run 10 times online and 10 times in a fully air-gapped configuration with no network access and literature served from a local 40-million-article MEDLINE mirror. Files: ..._supplemental_online_30runs_data.tar.gz and ..._supplemental_airgapped_30runs_data.tar.gz each contain 30 runs with reports (Markdown, PDF, HTML), all generated figures, per-iteration transcripts, the exact prompt, and full version/commit provenance. ..._supplemental_60runs_metrics.csv gives per-run runtime, tool-call counts, literature searches, findings recorded and token usage for all 60 runs. Version 3 (September 2026) adds two further supplementary sets for case study 3 (neurofibrillary tangle transcriptomics). ..._supplemental_reproducibility_10runs_data.tar.gz contains 10 independent runs of the same question on Claude Opus 4.6, all run on 2026-03-08 with byte-identical inputs (the research question and the input .h5ad were SHA-256 verified identical across all 10) and a 10-iteration budget. Each run includes the report (Markdown, PDF, HTML), knowledge_state.json with structured findings and literature list, per-iteration transcripts, and the job UUID. These runs quantify run-to-run variability under fixed inputs. ..._supplemental_genomic_skill_comparison_data.tar.gz contains 30 runs — 15 using the original genomics Agent Skill and 15 using a revised version — with the two skill definitions included alongside the jobs. The revised skill adds explicit guidance on donor-level pseudobulk aggregation and mixed-effect modelling; the paired arms allow the effect of that guidance on the analysis the agent chooses to be assessed directly. Each run includes reports (Markdown, PDF, HTML), per-iteration provenance transcripts, and container logs. Version 4 (October 2026) adds the run sets generated for the second revision of the manuscript, renumbers the case-study files to match the revised manuscript (the suvorexant proteomics analysis is now Case Study 5; neurofibromatosis is Case Study 6, drug side effects Case Study 7, and the CSF Aβ42/40 prediction model Case Study 8), and adds RUNS_MANIFEST.csv , which maps every job in this record to its experiment, supplementary table and row label. Run IDs quoted in the supplementary tables are the first 8 hexadecimal characters of the job ID. items.summary: Multimodal transformer models have driven unprecedented performance breakthroughs in modern document understanding. However, the inherent black-box nature of these models remains a major obstacle to their safe deployment in high-stakes sectors. Despite significant progress in explainability for vision and language tasks, explainable AI (XAI) research tailored to multimodal document understanding has received little attention. To address this gap, we present \ourframework{}, the first comprehensive explainability framework that adapts existing XAI methods and evaluation metrics to the multimodal (text, layout, and image) document understanding context, while introducing efficient multi-target adaptations of both methods and metrics for domain-specific tasks such as semantic entity recognition. Using \ourframework{}, we systematically evaluate 13 XAI methods across 3 document understanding tasks, 8 datasets, 4 models, and 17 evaluation metrics, and find that only a few methods perform consistently across all evaluation criteria, with Occlusion emerging as the most faithful and interpretable method overall. Through a dedicated meta-evaluation, we observe moderate to strong agreement among several faithfulness and complexity metrics while identifying certain ones that produce unreliable results. Finally, through multiple dataset-wide diagnostic analyses, we uncover key insights into model behavior, including the contribution of individual modalities across tasks and labels, spatial attribution patterns around target entities, and potential dataset biases. Overall, this work serves as both a benchmark and a practical guide for future XAI research in multimodal document understanding. To support reproducibility, we publicly release our code at https://github.com/saifullah3396/docxeval/.
items.title: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding

Pelletier, released publicly for the first time with this work and separately deposited at ORNL/OSTI doi:10.25983/PMI/3399550. - README.md with the full file-by-file description, dataset provenance, and reproduction instructions. items.summary: Early-warning models in learning analytics can identify learners at risk of failure or withdrawal, but the resulting alerts are often only weakly connected to inspectable learning evidence. A risk score may indicate that intervention is needed without showing which traces, assessment events, or temporal patterns justify the alert. This paper introduces an incremental Learner Digital Twin for evidence-grounded early warning, implemented as a lightweight knowledge graph. The twin is updated at temporal checkpoints by replaying learning traces and assessment records, and it serves both as a feature-extraction substrate and as an explanation-grounding substrate. Predictive features are derived through graph-mediated queries, while features, attributions, alerts, evidence items, and raw records are represented as queryable graph entities. The framework is instantiated and evaluated on a public learning-analytics benchmark under a temporal protocol. The results show that graph-mediated feature extraction preserves the predictive behavior of equivalent raw-table features across model families and checkpoints. Generated alerts are materialized as evidence chains linking risk decisions to feature attributions, evidence items, and raw platform records. The study shows that early-warning prediction can be routed through a semantic and provenance-aware representation while preserving predictive performance and adding traceability, verifiability, and evidence-grounded explanation.
items.title: An Incremental Knowledge-Graph Learner Digital Twin for Evidence-Grounded Early Warning

items.summary: We examine conditional charged-multiplicity fluctuations at fixed multiparton interaction (MPI) count in retained PYTHIA proton-proton samples at centre-of-mass energies of 2.76, 7, and 13 TeV. Charged particles satisfy |eta| < 0.8 and 0.15 < pT < 20 GeV/c. In the historical colour-reconnection (CR)-labelled baseline samples, the CR-ON conditional mean is smaller by a larger fraction than the standard deviation: the absolute width is smaller, while the coefficient of variation is larger in every retained matched MPI bin. Effective lifetime/decay settings and their per-run correspondence are unverified for this baseline, so these comparisons do not establish that CR alone causes the observed differences or their energy dependence. A separately documented 13 TeV comparison using the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) CP5 tune, with equal non-CR physics settings and particle data across the ON/OFF pair, exhibits the same absolute-versus-relative width ordering. Retained independent Monash and A14 samples also show this pattern, subject to historical production-record limitations. A comparison with mean-transverse-momentum data from A Large Ion Collider Experiment (ALICE) and simulated activity estimators provides final-state context within the stated particle-definition and provenance limits.
items.title: Color-Reconnection Effects on the nMPI-Nch Conditional Multiplicity Fluctuations in PYTHIA 8 pp Collisions

items.summary: A persistent belief in modern AI is that sufficiently large learners trained on sufficiently much data can make explicit domain knowledge optional. This paper examines a limitation of that belief. We define structure-encoded problems: tasks whose input-output map is determined, or sharply constrained, by known structure such as a solver, symmetry group, graph, physical law, measurement operator, grammar, combinatorial search space, or optimization objective. For such tasks, the central question is not expressivity--a dense neural network may contain the desired map--but finite-data identification, extrapolation, and certification. We introduce the structure gap: the finite-resource gap between a method that receives the governing structure and a learner that receives only examples. The strongest useful form of the claim is asymptotic rather than absolute: structure-agnostic learning may approach a structured solver as coverage grows, but every finite dataset can leave residual uncertainty that the structure resolves by construction. We prove this exactly for a Gaussian inverse problem: the known-operator Wiener solver attains Bayes risk, while the dense empirical learner in the correct linear class has persistent expected excess risk. We also prove a cell-coverage lower bound and an unobserved-orbit non-identifiability result. Controlled experiments in known-operator inversion, sparse recovery, and graph reachability with size extrapolation instantiate the mechanisms. When validated structure is available, it can constrain the hypothesis space before learning begins, leaving learning to address components the structure does not specify.
items.title: The Structure Gap: When More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning

items.summary: This paper is concerned with the simultaneous recovery of the trajectory and intensity of an unknown moving point source in an inhomogeneous acoustic medium. We prove that the whole-boundary measurements over a finite time interval uniquely determine the moving source. Furthermore, under suitable propagation and rank assumptions, Lipschitz stability of determining both the trajectory and intensity is derived using waveforms measured at four fixed receivers outside the source region. A novel Volterra--Euler reconstruction scheme is developed for solving the inverse problem, and the error estimate is derived for the proposed scheme. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed numerical method.
items.title: An inverse moving point source problem in inhomogeneous acoustic media: uniqueness, stability and reconstruction

items.summary: QIGONG BREATHING AND INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NEUROFEEDBACK COUPLING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition that constructs a falsifiable, explicitly nonclinical research program joining measured breathing tasks, cardiorespiratory and EEG feedback, and isolated microscale actuator surrogates. The central problem is not whether breathing changes heart-rate variability - that has established ordinary physiological explanations - but whether a proposed feedback architecture adds independently measurable predictive or benchtop-control value after breathing rate, phase, expectancy, ordinary cardiorespiratory dynamics, sensor calibration, stimulus timing and strong conventional controllers have been fairly matched. The primary hypothesis is deliberately narrow. A prospective factorial design separates a preregistered breathing condition from an isolated, non-human phantom-drive condition. Its interaction term, order effects, washout, hierarchical sampling units, pressure-related mechanisms and full-episode denominators are subjected to masked scheduling, matched sham sensory cues, covariance-aware uncertainty and independent laboratory reconstruction. Any apparent signal explained by paced breathing or cue entrainment is treated as a legitimate negative result. A bench interaction is not evidence of physiological effects from actual acupuncture in a person. Thirty mathematically differentiated research plates address factorial contrasts, hierarchical estimands, respiratory sinus arrhythmia, ECG event genealogy, pressure-respiration transfer, spectral coherence, lag and phase, multiple comparisons, uncertainty covariance, causal identification, feedback latency, safe-state projection, isolated charge and thermal constraints, abstention and provenance. Across 82 chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations, the book examines operational breathing definitions, reference instruments, EEG and ECG artifacts, blinded feedback protocols, mechanical and electrical phantoms, strong ordinary competitors, statistics, safety vetoes and reproducible handoff. Two hundred full-page Research Gates place their complete falsifiable research question in large deep-navy type, followed by an independently measurable outcome, adverse experiment, conventional physical rival and stopping rule. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinct successor objects ranging from calibration bridges and sham credibility tests to independent hardware vetoes, covariance sentinels, multisite reference capsules and protected null-result archives. An accompanying Excel index links formulas, chapters, Gates, candidate objects, citations and explicit evidence limitations. This work reports no executed integrated experiments, in-human needling, electrical stimulation, clinical efficacy, diagnosis or regulatory authorization. Its three STARLI mother-volume DOIs establish author research-method ancestry. Thirteen separately identified external research and metrology DOIs support established measurement, breathing physiology, neurofeedback reporting, uncertainty and statistical methodology, not the novel combined hypothesis. The 777-page layout, formula-clearance checks and 200 Gate color checks were automated; recurring editorial phrasing remains and full independent scientific peer review has not taken place. items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. When two copies of a system, one hotter and one cooler, relax in the same bath, the Markovian Mpemba effect is a crossing of their distances from equilibrium. This package gives a sufficient test that rules out such crossings at every time: if the dynamics and its time reverse preserve the cone of observables with nondecreasing arithmetic prefix means, cooling Gibbs preparations stay ordered for relative entropy (both orientations), squared Hellinger and Rényi divergences of order 0<α≤2, including for common schedules of noncommuting stages. For complete-graph bosonic population rates with common coupling, the test holds for every spectrum and bath temperature exactly when the spontaneous jump weight is concave; Ohmic baths with large enough cutoff, Drude–Lorentz and sub-Ohmic weights qualify on explicit ranges, super-Ohmic weights do not. A certified super-Ohmic example (J=d 3 ) shows an actual relative-entropy crossing. Limits: an exact five-state cone-preserving example has a brief total-variation reversal, and for every N≥4 there are N-level systems with a slow-mode inversion although no proper induced subsystem shows one. The archive contains the 27-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX), exact rational and interval certificates, a reproduction runner, semantic negative controls, CI and SHA-256 sums. Assurance: written proofs, exact certificates, internal AI-assisted review only (not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification); the closest antecedent (Avitan et al. 2026) already excludes the slow-mode effect for Ohmic and sub-Ohmic spectra. Creator: Anonymous. Text and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.
items.title: Thermal ordering under Markovian relaxation: a finite-time criterion and its limits

items.summary: System identification, namely the inference of mathematical representations of dynamical systems from measured data, is fundamental to engineering diagnostics, prognostics, and decision-making. Bayesian filtering offers a principled framework for probabilistic state estimation but traditionally relies on prescribed transition and observation models. Recent advances in deep Bayesian filtering address this limitation by embedding learnable representations within probabilistic state-space formulations, enabling data-driven identification of unknown dynamics while retaining physical structure and uncertainty-aware inference. This tutorial provides a systematic introduction to deep Bayesian filtering for nonlinear structural system identification, focusing on the interplay between learned dynamics, physical inductive biases, and posterior inference. The Deep Markov Model serves as a data-driven reference, while the Physics-guided Deep Markov Model (PgDMM) and Neural Extended Kalman Filter (Neural EKF) illustrate complementary approaches based on amortized variational inference and differentiable Kalman filtering, respectively. Their capabilities are examined through dynamic state estimation and joint dynamic state and parameter estimation on a three-dimensional shear-frame benchmark with hysteretic Bouc-Wen connections and sparse acceleration measurements. The results highlight important distinctions between measurement-conditioned reconstruction and open-loop forecasting, demonstrate how physical structure can improve latent-state interpretability without necessarily ensuring predictive fidelity, and reveal differences in the robustness of response and parameter estimation. Practical guidelines for model construction, training, evaluation, and deployment are provided, together with an outlook on remaining challenges in uncertainty calibration, identifiability, and real-world validation.
items.title: Deep Bayesian Approaches for Interpretable Nonlinear Structural System Identification

items.summary: Spectral-temporal unmixing of MODIS time series is essential for applications such as abundance mapping and spectral library construction, yet it remains challenging due to (i) spectral-temporal information coupling in MODIS data, (ii) intra-class endmember spectral variability and inter-class signature ambiguity, and (iii) the instability of naively fusing multiple expert representations. This paper presents the Multi- task Disentangling Fusion Mamba (MDF-Mamba) to address these limitations. To resolve spectral-temporal coupling, we design a disentangling architecture that pairs per-channel spectral experts with a dedicated bidirectional state-space (Mamba) temporal branch. Convolutional modules each process a single spectral channel, while the Mamba branch encodes the cross-channel seasonal trajectory, forming a multi-branch expert ensemble with soft inter-expert reweighting based on squeeze-and-excitation. For the integration of these spectral and temporal expert outputs, we introduce mHCFusion, adapting the manifold-constrained hyper-connection framework to merge the outputs in a stable and interpretable manner. Endmember variability is addressed by extending the linear mixing model with pixel-wise learnable spectral variability weights that capture intra-class endmember variation. Finally, we design a multi-task training objective that combines supervised abundance estimation with self-supervised spectral reconstruction and endmember regularization terms on the same training data, yielding a highly efficient framework for spectral-temporal unmixing. Experiments on MODIS time series covering the Alberta and Saskatchewan provinces show that MDF-Mamba achieves the best performance on 12 of 14 evaluation metrics across both datasets (7 of 7 on Alberta; 5 of 7 on Saskatchewan), ranking second on the remaining two.
items.title: Multi-task Disentangling Fusion Mamba-CNN for MODIS Spectral-Temporal Unmixing with Endmember Variability Modeling

items.summary: Sparse expert execution does not remove the stored states needed to adapt a mixture-of-experts language model. We present DuplexTune, a framework for replaying coupled hidden states through pretrained attention and expert modules. Trainable width bridges connect two residual streams to the backbone. Bridge warm-up precedes backbone adaptation, with router weights kept frozen. We analyze the implicit state-recovery equation and identify the convergence and replay conditions needed for reconstruction. On Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, the single-H800 evaluation reports 38.8 GB peak memory, versus 64.8 GB for supervised fine-tuning with checkpointing, and throughput of 25.1 versus 19.9 samples/s. DuplexTune achieves 67.2% MMLU, 75.6% GSM8K, and 7.69 MT-Bench, with a weaker multilingual score than the checkpointed baseline. The results characterize a configuration-dependent tradeoff among state storage, throughput, and adaptation quality.
items.title: DuplexTune: Coupled-State Replay for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Adaptation

items.summary: QIGONG BREATHING AND INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NEUROFEEDBACK COUPLING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition that constructs a falsifiable, explicitly nonclinical research program joining measured breathing tasks, cardiorespiratory and EEG feedback, and isolated microscale actuator surrogates. The central problem is not whether breathing changes heart-rate variability - that has established ordinary physiological explanations - but whether a proposed feedback architecture adds independently measurable predictive or benchtop-control value after breathing rate, phase, expectancy, ordinary cardiorespiratory dynamics, sensor calibration, stimulus timing and strong conventional controllers have been fairly matched. The primary hypothesis is deliberately narrow. A prospective factorial design separates a preregistered breathing condition from an isolated, non-human phantom-drive condition. Its interaction term, order effects, washout, hierarchical sampling units, pressure-related mechanisms and full-episode denominators are subjected to masked scheduling, matched sham sensory cues, covariance-aware uncertainty and independent laboratory reconstruction. items.summary: Transferring semantically typed tokens between heterogeneous blockchains (e.g. EVM and Cosmos ecosystems) raises two problems: semantic mixing, the loss of a token's domainspecific meaning in transit (e.g., CO2 removals issued under different methodologies), and atomicity despite divergent consensus and timing assumptions. We propose a bridge that addresses both. A deterministic indicator identity derived from cryptographic commitments, mirrored in class registries on both chains and checked at mint time, preventing semantic mixing by construction. For atomicity, we extend hash time-locked contracts (HTLCs) from two-party exchange to single-owner transfer with an automatic callback that burns the source escrow after a destination claim, and a protocol-minimum bounty that makes the fallback burn incentive-compatible even against adversarial senders. We machine-check the protocol's invariants with TLC (supply conservation fails without the rational-monitor assumption and holds with it) and validate a bidirectional prototype on Polygon and Neutron mainnets over Axelar GMP: fully automatic transfers with a median end-to-end latency of 97 s over 50 Polygon to Neutron transfers across 7 days (all completed by the on-chain automatic callback) and 93 s in the reverse direction, and semantic-validation overhead below 0.4% of messaging cost. We also document the integration failure modes of Cosmos originated messaging, whose dominant operational risk proves to be relay eligibility rather than latency.
items.title: An EVM-Cosmos Bridge for Atomic, Semantic-Preserving Transfer of Environmental Tokens

items.summary: This repository provides the source code, simulation datasets, computational benchmarks, numerical results, and reproducibility materials supporting Paper I of the Principle of Representation Integration for Stable Models (PRISM-M), prepared for the Journal of Computational Neuroscience . PRISM-M V4 is a minimal recurrent computational framework organized around five functional operations: Extraction, Compression, Integration, Stabilization, and Prediction/Action (ECISP). The implementation uses a single independently evolving recurrent state, with finite-precision quantization and explicitly defined information-processing transformations. The framework is intended to examine the functional organization of information processing, contextual integration, and memory stabilization within established recurrent and state-space dynamics. The repository includes the frozen V4 implementation, mathematical definitions, parameter configurations, experimental protocols, random seeds, simulation trajectories, statistical analyses, and comparative benchmarks involving autoregressive models (ARX), Kalman filtering, and recurrent neural networks. The deposited materials document the original parameter-landscape and stability analyses, targeted perturbation experiments, memory-retention studies (M1–M5), and additional computational experiments (V1–V5) evaluating noise robustness, adaptability, recovery, interference resistance, and information recoverability. Additional validation materials include information-matched representation controls, intrinsic-noise sensitivity analyses, and mathematical verification of contraction and perturbation equivalence. These retrospective analyses are distinguished from the original experimental protocols. The repository also contains the numerical datasets, figure files, supplementary materials, execution instructions, software dependencies, provenance records, and SHA-256 integrity checks associated with Figures 1–6 and Supplementary Figures S1–S4. Computational reproduction and numerical verification have been performed for the principal analyses. Complete automated regeneration of all final publication artwork and independent cross-platform verification remain outside the scope of the completed checks. The purpose of this deposit is to facilitate independent evaluation, computational reproduction, and further investigation of the PRISM-M V4 framework. The model is a theoretical computational implementation and does not constitute direct biological validation or demonstrate a new class of recurrent dynamics.

items.summary: Deploying LLM agents in specialized domains often require fine-grained task-specific procedures and knowledge a general model lacks, yet parameter training is costly and non-interpretable, and hand-engineered agent systems shift the cost to expert labor. Episodic memory updates at context level, but single agent adaptation struggles to alleviate cross-task interference, especially with complex tasks such as multi-application navigation or data pool analysis. Although multi-agent evolution alleviates this problem, existing methods lack clear definitions on update rules and rely on the backbone model to decide where and how much the system changes. This ill-scoped evolution makes learning follow the backbone's structural preferences rather than the observed failures: one backbone accumulates skills while another spawns agents. We present EMMA (structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent workflow synthesis), which treats the configuration of a multi-agent system (controller routing memory, specialists inheriting a generalist prompt, and per-step procedural skills) as episodic memory. EMMA makes the ownership and admissibility of updates explicit: a reflector assigns each diagnosed failure to the scope owning its correction and proposes one edit within it, and backbone-independent guards keep every accepted edit scoped, incremental and bounded. Across KramaBench, AppWorld and BBEH with five backbones and four baselines (ACE, GEPA, EvoMAS and ADAS), EMMA attains the best overall performance on every benchmark, up to 32.5% over the strongest baseline, maintains consistent improvements across backbones, and uses 17-38% fewer training executions than the most efficient baseline.
items.title: EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis

items.summary: Memory helps LLM-based multi-agent systems reuse experience, but stored advice can be flawed or applied in the wrong situation. Team-level success or failure alone cannot reliably show whether a memory needs correction or should not have been used. We propose DiscernMem, a training-free framework that improves both memory quality and memory use. To improve quality, Defect-Aware Memory Refinement (DMR) compares team executions with a single memory and with no memory, diagnoses rule defects, and tests repairs on current and earlier tasks to guard against losing previously useful behavior. To guide appropriate use, Boundary-Learning Meta-Memory (BLM) records each memory's past uses and effects, learning when its owner role should apply or avoid it based on task context and incoming messages. Together, these components help teams correct flawed experience while retaining useful rules that were applied incorrectly. Experiments with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on four benchmarks show that DiscernMem achieves the highest average score on AutoGen, CAMEL, and MacNet, exceeding the strongest reported baselines by 0.51-4.32 points. It leads on code generation and symbolic planning across all three systems, including a PDDL score of 37.71 versus 28.48 on CAMEL.
items.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: Early-warning models in learning analytics can identify learners at risk of failure or withdrawal, but the resulting alerts are often only weakly connected to inspectable learning evidence. A risk score may indicate that intervention is needed without showing which traces, assessment events, or temporal patterns justify the alert. This paper introduces an incremental Learner Digital Twin for evidence-grounded early warning, implemented as a lightweight knowledge graph. The twin is updated at temporal checkpoints by replaying learning traces and assessment records, and it serves both as a feature-extraction substrate and as an explanation-grounding substrate. Predictive features are derived through graph-mediated queries, while features, attributions, alerts, evidence items, and raw records are represented as queryable graph entities. The framework is instantiated and evaluated on a public learning-analytics benchmark under a temporal protocol. The results show that graph-mediated feature extraction preserves the predictive behavior of equivalent raw-table features across model families and checkpoints. Generated alerts are materialized as evidence chains linking risk decisions to feature attributions, evidence items, and raw platform records. The study shows that early-warning prediction can be routed through a semantic and provenance-aware representation while preserving predictive performance and adding traceability, verifiability, and evidence-grounded explanation.
items.title: An Incremental Knowledge-Graph Learner Digital Twin for Evidence-Grounded Early Warning

items.summary: Perceiving human body motion is critical for multimodal systems that understand and assist people. Yet current evaluations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) largely focus on objects, scenes, and coarse actions, leaving their ability to reason about the body itself poorly assessed. This is especially challenging from the egocentric perspective, in which the body is only partially visible and motion must be inferred from occluded and temporally distributed cues. We introduce SOMA, a benchmark for fine-grained body-motion understanding from egocentric video, comprising 1,632 human-verified questions across three capability axes: body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning. We evaluate 37 leading closed-source, open-source, and specialized egocentric MLLMs, complemented by an extensive human evaluation. We find that humans also find this task difficult from video alone (68.5% accuracy), yet clearly outperform the strongest MLLM (Qwen3.6-27B), which reaches 50.0% zero-shot accuracy. Our error analysis shows that MLLMs often misread the wearer's own body, misjudge events in time, and are prone to biases such as favoring the right hand or under-counting repetitions. To narrow the gap to human performance and support further progress, we introduce a training dataset of aligned video, body motion, and language supervision, and a multimodal baseline that jointly learns from these modalities. By identifying common failure modes and missing capabilities in current MLLMs, we hope SOMA will inspire future research on body-motion understanding and multimodal reasoning. Full benchmark, training data, and code will be released at: https://cnai.epfl.ch/soma
items.title: SOMA: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Egocentric Behavior and Body-Motion Understanding

items.summary: Enterprise email security protects employees behind a corporate mail gateway. The people most exposed to employment and support-impersonation scams - students and early-career job seekers - are contacted inside consumer platforms, where no gateway sees the message. We present a dependency-free, explainable detector that works at the level of the individual message and its sender, and a public benchmark for comparing such detectors under cheap adversarial transformation. The detector has four layers: (1) deterministic lookalike checks built on Unicode UTS #39 confusable skeletons, mixed-script detection, bounded edit distance, and brand-agnostic detection of a domain hidden inside a link host; (2) a logistic-regression sender scorer over 23 named features trained on a synthetic generator spanning eight brands (holdout F1 0.987); (3) a message-intent classifier, with a rule baseline and a prompt-injection-hardened LLM wrapper, that receives structured sender facts from the first two layers and whose impersonation verdicts are discounted deterministically only when the sender is verified or unremarkable, nothing sensitive is asked, links stay under the sender's control, and the body does not claim the platform's authority; and (4) a 76-message, brand-parametric benchmark with ten label-preserving adversarial variants and three model-paraphrased corpora, scored on per-layer recall, false-positive rate, injection hijack rate, and latency. On a paraphrased corpus frozen before a single evaluation, all three Layer 3 backends reach recall 1.00 in the fused pipeline, at FPR 0.03 for the rule baseline and Gemma 3 27B and 0.10 for Llama 3.1 8B, against 0.83/0.03, 1.00/0.07 and 1.00/0.47 for the same backends unfused: the sender layers are worth 17 points of recall to the rules and 37 points of FPR to the small model. The 8B model obeyed an appended injection on 6 of 46 attacks, each caught only by a deterministic overrule; the 27B model obeyed none. Three findings fall out: UTS #39 skeletons do not fold Cyrillic U+0442 or Greek U+03BA to ASCII, so skeleton equality alone misses a mixed-script brand lookalike; regex intent cues lose 33 points of recall to a single confusable glyph unless text is confusable-folded first; and negation must be handled at clause level with an exception for conditionals. Code, weights, corpora, and per-message verdict dumps are released under the MIT license.
items.title: Message-Level Detection of Support-Team and Recruiter Impersonation on Consumer Platforms: A Layered Detector and Adversarial Benchmark

items.summary: Security pipelines often fuse several data sources and protect a downstream model with a cross-source anomaly detector. Such detectors are usually judged by their clean false-positive rate and by how well they catch random corruption. Neither metric captures an adversary who controls some sources and targets a specific downstream decision. We propose a threat-quantification score, the \emph{task-conditioned visibility margin}, defined as the least detector evidence a manipulation must reveal per unit of harm to the downstream task. The margin has a closed form, takes about $85\,μ$s per certificate, yields a minimum-evidence attack, and identifies task-relevant directions the detector cannot see. On a 17-channel industrial telemetry benchmark, a detector that flags 82.8\% of random single-channel corruptions is first-order blind on 64.7\% of task/subset pairs in an audit of one- to four-channel subsets. Task-conditioned manipulations cause more than twice as many falsely reassuring errors as generic stealthy ones, and more of them evade the alarm on four of five splits, mainly at small budgets. Used to prioritize audits on held-out subsets, the margin finds a median of four verified failures in ten checks, compared with none for random order and two for alarm-based ranking, and performs comparably to the task-gradient baseline. It also ranks vulnerable configurations of the learned GDN and TranAD detectors and of a five-source crop-yield panel.
items.title: Quantifying and Prioritizing Stealthy Source-Manipulation Threats Against Multi-Source Anomaly Detectors

items.summary: QIGONG BREATHING AND INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NEUROFEEDBACK COUPLING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition that constructs a falsifiable, explicitly nonclinical research program joining measured breathing tasks, cardiorespiratory and EEG feedback, and isolated microscale actuator surrogates. The central problem is not whether breathing changes heart-rate variability - that has established ordinary physiological explanations - but whether a proposed feedback architecture adds independently measurable predictive or benchtop-control value after breathing rate, phase, expectancy, ordinary cardiorespiratory dynamics, sensor calibration, stimulus timing and strong conventional controllers have been fairly matched. The primary hypothesis is deliberately narrow. A prospective factorial design separates a preregistered breathing condition from an isolated, non-human phantom-drive condition. Its interaction term, order effects, washout, hierarchical sampling units, pressure-related mechanisms and full-episode denominators are subjected to masked scheduling, matched sham sensory cues, covariance-aware uncertainty and independent laboratory reconstruction. Any apparent signal explained by paced breathing or cue entrainment is treated as a legitimate negative result. A bench interaction is not evidence of physiological effects from actual acupuncture in a person. Thirty mathematically differentiated research plates address factorial contrasts, hierarchical estimands, respiratory sinus arrhythmia, ECG event genealogy, pressure-respiration transfer, spectral coherence, lag and phase, multiple comparisons, uncertainty covariance, causal identification, feedback latency, safe-state projection, isolated charge and thermal constraints, abstention and provenance. Across 82 chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations, the book examines operational breathing definitions, reference instruments, EEG and ECG artifacts, blinded feedback protocols, mechanical and electrical phantoms, strong ordinary competitors, statistics, safety vetoes and reproducible handoff. Two hundred full-page Research Gates place their complete falsifiable research question in large deep-navy type, followed by an independently measurable outcome, adverse experiment, conventional physical rival and stopping rule. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinct successor objects ranging from calibration bridges and sham credibility tests to independent hardware vetoes, covariance sentinels, multisite reference capsules and protected null-result archives. An accompanying Excel index links formulas, chapters, Gates, candidate objects, citations and explicit evidence limitations. This work reports no executed integrated experiments, in-human needling, electrical stimulation, clinical efficacy, diagnosis or regulatory authorization. Its three STARLI mother-volume DOIs establish author research-method ancestry. Thirteen separately identified external research and metrology DOIs support established measurement, breathing physiology, neurofeedback reporting, uncertainty and statistical methodology, not the novel combined hypothesis. The 777-page layout, formula-clearance checks and 200 Gate color checks were automated; recurring editorial phrasing remains and full independent scientific peer review has not taken place. items.summary: BIOELECTRIC FEEDBACK AND PERSONALIZED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE CONTROL AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page prospective nonclinical research monograph on the boundary between measured bioelectric variability, personalized feedback algorithms, and genuinely verified safe closed-loop operation on inert phantoms and isolated bench hardware. Its primary question is whether a controller calibrated on limited reference data retains a meaningful improvement for entirely unseen simulated individuals while meeting hard, independently witnessed limits. The governing design separates physiological sensing, identification of individual model parameters, selection of feedback commands, and observed physical outcomes. The inherited objective is corrected to a unit-consistent normalized tracking loss and separately measured bench-output burden; no mathematical optimum can compensate a failed hardware veto, force cap, thermal boundary, or missing permission record. A synthetic dummy-output budget is explicitly not a clinical stimulation dose or therapeutic recommendation. Thirty differentiated mathematical plates explore covariance-aware metrology, personal and hierarchical system identification, robust model predictive control, posterior coverage, safe-set feasibility, population shift, abstention, actuator latency, thermal loading, physical isolation, state-space reachability, distributional tail risk and independent requalification. Each plate states construction assumptions, native units, blind tests, stop conditions and a crosswalk to relevant chapters and successor gates. Eighty-two chapters, each with five separately paginated studies, develop electrode and reference calibration, timebase reliability, individual parameter uncertainty, adversarial new-person transfer, fair PID and classical MPC comparisons, closed-loop constraints, sham feedback, safety engineering and handoff to an unrelated laboratory. Two hundred full-page Research Gates are designed as distinctly falsifiable future entry points, including blind reconstruction, strong conventional rivals and external adversarial continuation. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose different metrology tools, decision records, baseline devices or smaller successor theories that can survive disproof of the larger control claim. The three author mother-volume version DOIs are M1 10.5281/zenodo.23480803, M2 10.5281/zenodo.23486020 and M3 10.5281/zenodo.23318840. Separately identified published external DOI studies on neural decoding, population generalization, system identification, control and neurostimulation provide context only: none demonstrates this F47 integrated apparatus. This is a Research Working Edition, not an executed laboratory study, clinical trial, review approval or evidence of therapeutic benefit. Future human stimulation, puncture, clinical research and patient-facing equipment require their own independent regulatory and ethics program. items.summary: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.
items.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
